name: behavior check (Slot 5 VERIFY) and three tooling changes
status: PROPOSED - not locked, nothing built yet
why: Everything so far proves the result compiles and the connection exists. Nothing runs the scene. Godot only reports a handler/signal argument mismatch at emit time, so no current guard can see it.

slot5_verify.placement: APPLY -> RELOAD -> VERIFY -> (add_method only) REGISTRY refresh. A verify failure restores the .bak exactly like a failed reload.

per_op.connect_signal: run the probe on the signal and handler (below); the expectation comes from the handler's body
per_op.add_method: call the new function directly on the host node with type-default arguments; the expectation comes from the body that was just written
per_op.modify_property: unchanged: the reload check already reads the value back

flags: --verify-only (run the check on blocks that are already applied; no mule, no writes)
slot5_verify.ledger: row.verify = {mode, natural, explicit, emissions, effect, errors_mine, errors_other, verdict}

verdicts.PASS: the expected effect appeared in the normal run and not in the control run, and no error belongs to this connection
verdicts.FAIL: an expected effect is missing, or the control run shows the same effect (it did not come from the connection), or an error names this signal or handler
verdicts.UNVERIFIED: the handler body is not pass/print/assignment (for example hand-written): emission and errors are still checked, the effect is not asserted

probe.runs_in: one headless Godot process, about 0.27 s (the reload check alone is 0.18 s)
inputs: registered property names of the host
steps: instantiate the scene twice: 'normal' keeps the connection, 'control' has the handler disconnected before anything runs
attach a spy to the signal; snapshot the registered properties (pre)
enter the tree and wait one frame, then leave the tree and wait one frame; stdout between VERIFY>> and VERIFY<< markers belongs to that run
if the spy saw no natural emission, add the node and call emit_signal(<signal>, <type-default arguments>) explicitly (false, 0, 0.0, '', zero vectors, black, null)
snapshot again (post); print one JSON result; quit
probe.effect: effect = (normal run) minus (control run): printed lines, property changes, errors. Noise that appears in both runs (other connections, physics) cancels out.

expectations_from_the_handler_body.pass: no printed line, no property change, no error
expectations_from_the_handler_body.print(\"msg\"): the line 'msg' appears more often in the normal run than in the control run, and no property changes
expectations_from_the_handler_body.<property> = <literal> (step 10): that property differs between pre and post in the normal run only, and equals the literal

probe.errors: lines starting ERROR or SCRIPT ERROR inside the markers. An error that names this signal or this handler is mine (FAIL). Any other is reported as a warning about another connection in the scene.

registry_additions.signal_args: per signal: the list of argument types (ClassDB.class_get_signal_list and the script's signals)
registry_additions.method_args: per script method: its argument count (get_script_method_list)
registry_additions.GI_1_arity_rule: connect_signal is refused when the signal's argument count differs from the handler's argument count
registry_additions.note: v1 add_method args are bool/int/float/String/Vector2/Vector3/Color only, so signals that carry an object (child_entered_tree, input_event, ...) stay out of reach until args allow Node

item_1_patch_tooling.cascade_patchlib.py: one small shared library: a patch is a list of per-file entries {file, marker, edits}; for each file it decides done (marker present), ready (every anchor found exactly once) or blocked (names the anchors that are missing)
item_1_patch_tooling.behaviour: ready files are applied with a backup, done files are skipped, blocked files are reported with the exact missing anchors; one blocked file never stops the others; re-running the patch finishes whatever is left
item_1_patch_tooling.patch_status.py: read-only: prints, for every known patch, the state of each file it touches (done / ready / blocked / not applicable)
item_1_patch_tooling.clock_self_check: the clock lists the ops it has code for; at GI-1, if the spec lacks one of them it says 'the spec is behind the clock: run patch_status.py' instead of a list of missing slots
item_1_patch_tooling.scope: all new patches (Step 9 onward) use the library; the old ones are already applied and patch_status.py reads their markers

item_3_multiple_blocks.cli: python cascade_clock.py a.json b.json c.json   (blocks run in the order given, one process, Gemma loaded once)
item_3_multiple_blocks.between_blocks: spec, registry and scene are re-read for every block, so the registry refresh after add_method is visible to the connect_signal that follows
item_3_multiple_blocks.on_failure: the chain stops at the first block that is not ACK/APPLIED/NOOP; --keep-going continues; the exit code is the first failing block's code
item_3_multiple_blocks.output: one summary table at the end: block, op, status, tries, seconds
item_3_multiple_blocks.GI_2: the VRAM measurement is taken before the first block loads the model and is not repeated for later blocks in the same process (the loaded model itself sits near 10 GB and tripped the guard in the sweeps); the RAM-cache rule is still checked each time

natural_signals.note: signals fire after the first frame when the node is added from _initialize, and ready fires once per instance (so the control must be a fresh instance)

tested_on_godot_4_3.arity_mismatch: ERROR: Error calling from signal 'child_entered_tree' to callable ...: Method expected 0 arguments, but called with 1. Raised at emit time only; the parse check, the reload check and the connection list all miss it. A natural signal (child_entered_tree) hit it with no explicit emit.

probe_prototype_results.tree_exiting -> print handler: normal run printed bye once, control printed nothing; one emission, natural
probe_prototype_results.renamed -> assignment handler: never fires by itself; the explicit emit changed speed 300 -> 450 in the normal run and nothing in the control run
probe_prototype_results.child_entered_tree -> 0-argument handler: normal run: 1 error naming the signal and handler; control run: 0 errors

tested_on_godot_4_3.direct_call: calling a function on the host prints its output between the markers, which is the add_method observable
